title: Napoleon's retreat from Moscow, 1812 — he came with an empire's army and left on a sled
sources: Wikipedia: French invasion of Russia — Napoleon's initial force exceeded 450,000 men and 150,000 horses; on 14 September 1812 he entered Moscow and found it deserted and set ablaze by its military governor Rostopchin; as early November arrived, snowfall and frost complicated the retreat; shortages of food, winter clothing and fodder, and attacks by Russian peasants and Cossacks, caused huge losses; starving soldiers cut up horses that fell, even before they were dead; by the Berezina Napoleon commanded only around 49,000 troops alongside 40,000 stragglers; on 5 December he left the army at Smorgonie in a sled and returned to Paris; the army was beaten at Maloyaroslavets, Vyazma and Krasnoi on the way out

Wikipedia: Battle of Berezina — General Eblé, commander of the bridge builders, had disobeyed Napoleon's orders to destroy the bridging equipment and tools; the river was full of drifting ice and pontoon bridges had to be built; Napoleon ordered the bridges burned in the morning, and Eblé delayed the order
Wikipedia On This Day (11-03): 1812, Napoleon's armies are defeated at the Battle of Vyazma
Also on this day (candidates.md, in the app): 1957 Sputnik 2 carries the dog Laika into orbit; 1793 Olympe de Gouges is guillotined

Paintings and chart (public domain): Adolph Northen, Napoleon's Retreat from Moscow; Albrecht Adam, Napoleon in Burning Moscow (1841) and the Berezina crossing (1830); Lawrence Alma-Tadema, the Berezina; Christian Faber du Faur, Smarhoń, 3 December 1812; Zygmunt Rozwadowski, Napoleon at Smorgonie; Jerzy Kossak; Vereshchagin, Napoleon near Borodino; Alfred Wierusz-Kowalski; Charles Minard's 1869 chart of the army's losses
Illustrative stock footage (Pexels, free licence; not of the event): snowfall, a winter forest at night, a frozen river, a fire in the snow

post.facebook:
On this day in 1812, Napoleon's retreating army was beaten at Vyazma.

He had invaded Russia with more than 450,000 men. In September he took Moscow — and found it deserted and on fire, set ablaze by its own governor. With no peace and no supplies, the Grand Army turned for home. Then, in early November, came the snow and the frost.

There was no winter clothing, no food, no fodder. Cossacks and peasants attacked the columns. When a horse fell, starving soldiers cut it up before it had even died. At the Berezina river, full of drifting ice, the army was trapped — and it was saved by General Eblé, who had disobeyed Napoleon's order to destroy his bridge-building tools.

By then only about 49,000 fighting men were left. On 5 December, Napoleon left the army behind and rode for Paris in a sled.

Also on 3 November: Laika went into orbit aboard Sputnik 2 (1957), and Olympe de Gouges was guillotined (1793).

youtube.description:
3 November 1812: Napoleon's retreating Grand Army was beaten at Vyazma. He had invaded Russia with more than 450,000 men, found Moscow empty and burning, and turned for home with no supplies — straight into the snow and frost. Horses died, Cossacks attacked, and at the icy Berezina the army was saved only by General Eblé, who had disobeyed orders and kept his bridge-building tools. About 49,000 fighting men were left. In December, Napoleon rode for Paris in a sled.

Also on 3 November: Laika and Sputnik 2 (1957) and Olympe de Gouges (1793).
